summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, Litian Fang studied at Peking University under Feng Youlan, Yongtong Tang, and Zhang Dainian (~1956–1961). He served at Renmin University of China as professor, doctoral supervisor, and founding director (~1961–2014).

Liz Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned her PhD from the University of Chicago (1985–1992). She was a lecturer at the University of Chicago (1991–1992) and became Associate Professor of Religion at Miami University in 1992.
Specializing in religious studies, Liza Zigmund-Cerbu studied in 1947 at both the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales.

Ljudmila Aleksandrovna Aganina worked in Indology and linguistics. She served in the editorial office of Sovetskoe vostokovedenie (1954–1958) and was a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1958.

Ljudmila Aleksandrovna Mervart, an Indology and linguistics scholar, studied at Saint Petersburg State University (1910). Her posts included Far Eastern Federal University (1918–1923), Kunstkamera (~1918–1930), Institute of Ethnology and Anthropology (1924–1944), Military Institute of Foreign Languages (1945–1948), and Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1949–1958).

Lloyd W. Pflueger, active in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, earned a doctorate from the University of California, Santa Barbara. He is attested in 2015 as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University.

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, Lobsang Choedak earned an Acharya degree at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2012–2013). He worked at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (2013–2018) and lectured at CIHTS in 2018.
Lobsang Dargyay specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Munich (~1969–1974).

Lobsang Gyatso worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Drepung Monastery (~1940–1959) and under Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso. He founded the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (1973), which he headed until 1997, and founded the College for Higher Tibetan Studies (1991).

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Lozang Jamspal studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Columbia University under Alex Wayman. His appointments included Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, University of Delhi (attested 1973), and Columbia University (attested 1985–1990).

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa studied under numerous masters, including Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Shukseb Jetsun Choying Zangmo, and Drubwang Shakya Shri.

Lobsang Shastri works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Head Librarian at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

Working in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Lobsang Tendzin studied at Drepung Monastery (1951) and Gyuto Monastery (-1970). He held leadership roles at the Central Schools for Tibetans (1961–1970) and served as director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1988–2000).

Lobsang Tenpa specializes in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He earned a Master of Philosophy under the supervision of Sharad K. Soni at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

A Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Drepung Monastery, Lobsang Tenzin served as principal/religious teacher at Central Schools for Tibetans (1961–1970), principal and director of CIHTS (1971; 1988–2001), abbot of Gyume Tantric College (1987), and chancellor of Sanchi University.

Lobsang Yongdan, a Tibetology and history scholar, studied at Kumbum Monastery and completed a PhD at the University of Cambridge (-2014) under Hildegard Diemberger. He held research positions at Cambridge, MPIWG (2016), University of Bonn (2016–2020), and Austrian Academy of Sciences (2021–2026).

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Loden Sherab Dagyab studied at Drepung Monastery and under Trijang Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama. He served as director of Tibet House New Delhi (1964–1966) and worked at the University of Bonn (1966).
Lodrö Chökyi Sengé studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche, and also served as a teacher to Kalu Rinpoche.
Lodrö Sangpo works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner, founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996, and served as a senior teacher at Gampo Abbey (attested 2008).

Lokesh Chandra specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, studying at the University of the Punjab and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He served as secretary and director of the International Academy of Indian Culture (~1950–2022) and chaired the ICCR and ICHR.
